name: Wampanoag
region: Southern New England; present-day Massachusetts and Rhode Island.
bio: Ousamequin was a Pokanoket sachem within the Wampanoag world. A 1623 account describes a broad wampum belt and a black wolfskin over his shoulder.
note: Use Narragansett as a scenario rival inspired by early seventeenth-century regional tensions; alliances also changed over time.
flag: A rising sun above two coastal waves. A new landscape-based game emblem, not a historical national flag.

name: Powhatan
region: Tidewater Virginia and the Chesapeake coastal plain.
bio: Wahunsenacawh was the paramount chief known to the English as Powhatan. He led a chiefdom of multiple communities when Jamestown was founded in 1607.
note: Monacan is a documented regional rival. Food reflects maize agriculture; Tobacco is a simplified game category for Indigenous tobacco, not a European plantation uniform.
flag: Maize above a branching river on rust red. New game emblem inspired by Tidewater agriculture and waterways.

name: Onondaga (Haudenosaunee)
region: Central present-day New York; Great Lakes and northeastern woodlands.
bio: Garakontie was an Onondaga chief and important seventeenth-century diplomat. He represents Onondaga here, not an absolute monarch of all Haudenosaunee nations.
note: Wendat rivalry references seventeenth-century Haudenosaunee-Wendat conflicts; Garakontie's own career also included sustained peace negotiations.
flag: One longhouse on a deep purple field. Original architectural emblem; not a reproduction of the Hiawatha Belt or a modern Haudenosaunee flag.

name: Wendat
region: Great Lakes region; Kondiaronk's community was associated with Michilimackinac.
bio: Kondiaronk was a Tionontati-Wendat leader and diplomat. This c. 1690 depiction precedes his major role in the Great Peace of Montreal in 1701.
note: The faction uses the broad Wendat label with Kondiaronk's Tionontati background stated explicitly. Haudenosaunee is a historical scenario rival, not a permanent enemy.
flag: A canoe and paired paddles on dark teal, referencing Great Lakes travel. Original game emblem.

name: Lenape
region: Delaware Valley; present-day Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Delaware and nearby areas.
bio: Tamanend was a Lenape village sachem documented in late seventeenth-century Pennsylvania. He was not a king ruling all Lenape communities.
note: Susquehannock rivalry refers to earlier conflicts in the 1620s-1630s, not a claim that Tamanend fought them in 1683. Food and Fur match farming and winter hunting.
flag: Two leaves flanking a river on forest green. Original landscape emblem, not a Lenape clan or tribal seal.

name: Narragansett
region: Narragansett Bay and present-day Rhode Island.
bio: Miantonomi was a Narragansett sachem active in the early seventeenth century. His recorded speech is a source for understanding Indigenous responses to colonial expansion.
note: Pequot rivalry refers to the Pequot War period of 1636-1638, before this approximate portrait date. Tobacco Planters is a game abstraction for local cultivation.
flag: A stylized shell above coastal waves on indigo. New game emblem referring to coastal resources and shell working.

name: Pequot
region: Coastal southeastern Connecticut and adjacent southern New England.
bio: Sassacus was a Pequot sachem during the 1630s. The village design uses bark-covered dwellings and a palisade associated with fortified settlements of the period.
note: Mohegan is a scenario rival in the context of the Pequot War. High aggression is solely an editable AI balance setting, not a characterization of Pequot people.
flag: A palisade gateway on ochre with a red central panel. Original emblem inspired by settlement architecture.

name: Mexica (Aztec)
region: Basin of Mexico; Tenochtitlan and the wider Mexica tribute network.
bio: Moctezuma II was the Mexica tlatoani at the arrival of Cortes in 1519. The city icon uses masonry buildings, twin temple shrines, canals and chinampa gardens.
note: Cotton includes exchange and tribute from warmer regions; it does not imply cotton plantations in the highland capital. Tlaxcalteca is a documented rival polity.
flag: Stepped garden geometry over water on turquoise. Original landscape emblem; not Mexico's modern eagle flag or a claimed Aztec national flag.
